message.content: Trade impacted the pharaoh's powers because it gave them wealth, made their armies stronger, allowed their scribes to keep records, showed they controlled Egypt, made their temples richer, and made their gods appear more powerful. We can see that, when they had copper, timber, and spices, they could pay workers, reward nobles, and impress outsiders. Their caravans proved that the state protected them; their taxes filled their granaries; their priests used those goods for festivals, and we know that it raised their prestige. If they failed to manage trade, people saw weakness, rivals attacked, and their authority fell. So it helped make them more powerful, but it also made their power depend on other regions, other people, and other systems.
